steps: Enthalpy (H) is the total heat content of a system at constant pressure.
Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the difference between the enthalpy of the products and the enthalpy of the reactants.
At constant pressure, enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released during a process.
items.finalAnswer: Enthalpy is the heat content of a system; enthalpy change is the difference between the enthalpies of products and reactants.

steps: Energy is required to overcome the attractive forces between the atoms joined by a bond.
Therefore, bond breaking absorbs energy from the surroundings and is an endothermic process.
items.finalAnswer: Breaking a bond is endothermic because energy must be absorbed to overcome the attraction between the bonded atoms.

items.figure: Show H₂ and Cl₂ approaching. Draw the activated complex as [H₂Cl₂]‡, with the H–H and Cl–Cl bonds partly broken and the two H–Cl bonds partly formed. Show the products as 2HCl.
steps: Draw H₂ and Cl₂ as the reactant molecules approaching one another.
Show a transition-state complex, [H₂Cl₂]‡, in which the H–H and Cl–Cl bonds are partly broken and H–Cl bonds are partly formed.
Show the products as two HCl molecules.
items.finalAnswer: The transition state is the activated complex [H₂Cl₂]‡, with old bonds partly broken and new H–Cl bonds partly formed.

items.figure: Draw a graph with energy on the vertical axis and reaction progress on the horizontal axis. Begin both curves at the same reactant energy and end them at a lower product energy. Draw a higher peak for the slower reaction and a lower peak for the faster reaction. Label the peaks’ heights from the reactant level as activation energies, with the faster reaction having the lower activation energy.
steps: Draw and label the vertical axis Energy and the horizontal axis Reaction progress.
Draw two reaction profiles that start at the same reactant energy and finish at a lower product energy; both reactions are exothermic.
Draw a higher activation-energy peak for the slower reaction and a lower activation-energy peak for the faster reaction.
Label the curves Slow reaction and Fast reaction.
items.finalAnswer: The faster exothermic reaction has the lower activation energy; both profiles have products at lower energy than the reactants.

steps: Glycogen is the storage form of carbohydrate in the body.
It is stored mainly in the liver and muscles.
When the body needs energy, glycogen is broken down to glucose.
items.finalAnswer: Glycogen stores carbohydrate in the liver and muscles and can be broken down to glucose when energy is needed.

steps: Conversion of a hydrated salt into an anhydrous salt is endothermic.
Conduction of electricity by metals is exothermic.
